title: Gate: PR #34 review findings (skill-chooser ADR)
description:
Human review gate collecting wonderbird's review findings on PR #34 (skill-chooser branch), covering ADR 002 and project-template/docs/manage-skills.md. Each finding is a child task.

IMPORTANT: This gate MUST NOT be closed by an AI agent. Only the human reviewer may close it, after verifying that each child finding has been properly addressed.

title: F3: verify & correct GitHub Copilot agent-skills claims in ADR 002
description:
PR #34 comment on docs/architecture-decisions/002-skill-manager-tool-selection.md:100.

Reviewer: the GitHub Copilot instructions info seems outdated. Verify against https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/agents/about-agent-skills and reconsider. Update the following paragraphs accordingly.

Impact: if Copilot now supports an agent-skills (SKILL.md-style) concept rather than only .github/instructions/*.instructions.md, the ADR's 'file-based Copilot needs generation / no tool emits it' framing is partly wrong and recurs in Context, Consequences, Open questions, and several option analyses. CORRECTNESS-FIRST: resolve before the size-reduction findings (F1/F2/F6) trim dependent text. Requires fetching and verifying the linked doc.

title: F4: correct agent target-dir claims (Antigravity uses .agents) in ADR 002
description:
PR #34 comment on docs/architecture-decisions/002-skill-manager-tool-selection.md:106.

Reviewer: at least the Antigravity CLI also uses the agent-skills standard folder .agents. Check https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills and double-check whether other tools in this ADR need correction too.

Impact: the ADR lists Antigravity as ~/.gemini/config/skills; verify against the vercel-labs agents table and fix any other 'nominal/hardcoded-target' claims that are actually .agents-standard. CORRECTNESS-FIRST.

title: F1: reduce overall ADR 002 size for experienced-developer audience
description:
PR #34 comment on docs/architecture-decisions/002-skill-manager-tool-selection.md:1 (whole-document, umbrella).

Reviewer: the document is very large and a hard burden for a human reader. Walk through and ultrathink: which information is redundant and removable or replaceable by a link? Which is not required to understand the decision? Audience = experienced software developers; leave out or simplify accordingly to reduce size.

Note: umbrella finding; F2 (exec summary), F6 (line 270 section), F7 (README-duplicated block) are concrete instances. Do this pass AFTER F3/F4 correctness fixes so trimmed text does not need rewriting.

title: Human review: verify fixes for ai-agent-workspace-lqd findings; invoke /record-findings ai-agent-workspace-lqd
description:
IMPORTANT: This task MUST be executed by the human reviewer, not an AI agent, and MUST NOT be closed by an AI agent.

Review procedure — derive everything live; trust no pre-baked list or order:
1. List the gate's children (open AND closed) via 'br show ai-agent-workspace-lqd', then exclude any already labeled 'human-reviewed' and this review task itself. What remains is the unreviewed set.
2. For each finding in the unreviewed set, locate its fixing commit(s) with 'git log --no-pager --grep=<finding-id>' (the commit skill mandates a 'Refs: <finding-id>' trailer, so every fix is discoverable). A finding with no commit is 'not yet fixed' — leave it unlabeled for a later round.
3. From the files actually changed across those commits, group findings by file/area and order them dependency-first (computed in hindsight from the real diffs) so each file opens once. For a large/tangled set, delegate this ordering to a high-reasoning read-only subagent; skip delegation for a small set.
4. Walk through each finding in that order, confirming each fix. The moment the human accepts OR rejects a fix, mark it reviewed: 'br update <finding-id> --add-label human-reviewed'. For a rejected fix, also file a new child finding under the gate (stays unlabeled, reviewed next round).
